name: msgspec
workload: Decoding/validating JSON (and MessagePack/YAML/TOML) messages into typed Python objects (msgspec.Struct) compared against Pydantic v1/v2, cattrs, mashumaro, attrs/dataclasses, on the author's own machine with CPython 3.11.
claimed_speedup: ~6x faster than mashumaro, ~10x faster than cattrs, ~12x faster than Pydantic v2, ~85x faster than Pydantic v1; struct instance creation ~4x faster than dataclasses/attrs and ~17x faster than Pydantic
hardware: author states benchmarks were run on 'a ~2020 x86 Linux laptop' with CPython 3.11 -- no specific CPU model named
tradeoffs: Requires modeling data with msgspec.Struct/dataclass/TypedDict rather than arbitrary classes; validation happens inline during decode rather than as a separately customizable pass, so it has a smaller validator/coercion ecosystem than Pydantic; Python-only (C extension), not usable from C++; not compared against Boost.Serialization or cereal, or any C++ library.
caveats: First-party benchmark; hardware is described only as 'a ~2020 x86 Linux laptop', not a named CPU model, and no compiler/flags concept applies to the CPython interpreter used -- per the rubric this caps the entry at Tier C even though benchmark code is publicly linked. Numbers are self-reported by the author, not independently reproduced. Baseline (Pydantic) is not Boost.Serialization/cereal; recorded as the closest widely-used incumbent for a reflection-vs-codegen serialization comparison.
found_via: Hacker News: query 'fast serialization library' -> 'Show HN: Msgspec, a fast serialization/validation library for Python' (HN 35904386) and 'Msgspec: A fast and friendly serialization library for Python' (HN 33947949); benchmark numbers confirmed at https://msgspec.dev/benchmarks

name: ffjson
workload: Marshaling and unmarshaling Go structs to/from JSON using ffjson-generated static MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON functions instead of encoding/json's runtime reflection-based codec.
claimed_speedup: MarshalJSON 2x to 3x faster than encoding/json; UnmarshalJSON 2x to 3x faster than encoding/json
tradeoffs: Requires a codegen step (the ffjson tool, typically via go:generate) that must be re-run whenever struct definitions change; silently falls back to encoding/json (losing the speedup) for types it doesn't understand, such as interface fields, custom marshalers, inline structs, or nested slices/maps.
caveats: README states only a '2x to 3x' range with no benchmark code, dataset, Go version, or hardware disclosed. The original numbers trace to a 2014 blog post and have not been refreshed since. Repository has had no pushes since 2023-09-21 (over 3 years as of this run), so treat the claim as historical rather than reflecting current Go/encoding-json performance.
found_via: Hacker News: query 'Show HN serialization' -> 'ffjson: faster json serialization in Go' (HN 7501891, journal.paul.querna.org blog post, cross-checked against the current GitHub README)
